instructions: Drain the jackfruit and rinse it well under cold water. Squeeze each piece dry with your hands, then cut off any hard core pieces and pull the rest apart into chunky shreds.
Mince the garlic and grate the ginger together. Peel and finely chop the onion. Finely chop the tomatoes.
In a bowl, toss the jackfruit with 1/4 tsp of the turmeric, 1/4 tsp of the chili powder, the kasuri methi, 1/2 tsp of the garam masala, 1/4 tsp of the salt and half of the garlic and ginger.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the jackfruit and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the edges are browned. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp oil to the same skillet over medium heat. Add the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the onion and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until golden brown. Don't rush it. That's where the flavor starts.

Add the rest of the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in the remaining 1/2 tsp turmeric, the remaining 1/2 tsp chili powder, the coriander powder and the cumin powder. Cook for 20 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes, mashing them with your spoon, until they break down and the oil shows at the edges.
Return the jackfruit to the skillet and add 1 cup of water. Cover and simmer on low for 10 minutes, until it's tender and the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining 1/4 tsp garam masala and the cilantro. The whole spices stay in the pot, so tell anyone serving that they're not meant to be eaten.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with roti, naan or rice.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (the lead) marinates young jackfruit in curd, fries it, then simmers it in an onion and tomato masala built on whole spices. The other pages differ: Nisha Madhulika makes a cashew and tomato gravy, and Archana's adds potatoes and pressure cooks. This version uses canned young jackfruit, which Hebbar's says works, and skips the curd marinade (the author calls it optional) so it stays vegan and dairy-free. Instead the jackfruit is browned with the marinade spices. The cloves are cut from 7 to 4 and the chili halved to keep the base mild.
